reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch trace the thirty-talent gap to scribal confusion between two similar Hebrew numeral letters, explaining Kings' 420 against Chronicles' 450.

sides.snippet: gold, four hundred and twenty talents
sides.verseText: They came to Ophir, and fetched from there gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.

sides.snippet: four hundred fifty talents of gold
sides.verseText: Huram sent him by the hands of his servants ships, and servants who had knowledge of the sea; and they came with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, and fetched from there four hundred fifty talents of gold, and brought them to king Solomon.
